thread.title: Stock Market Higher On Fed Chair Jerome Powell; Palo Alto Breaks Out

author: SCOTT LEHTONEN
title: Stock Market Higher On Fed Chair Jerome Powell; Palo Alto Breaks Out
text:
The stock market looked to cap off its week with a solid gain Friday, gaining strength in morning trade. Fed Chair Jerome Powell commented that he expects gradual interest rate hikes ahead with a strong economy. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite is hanging out just below a record high. Top growth stock Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) is breaking out again today — according to MarketSmith chart analysis — while IPO stock BJ's Wholesale Club ( BJ ) followed through on Thursday's breakout. ( For updates on this story and other market coverage, visit the Stock Market Today .)
X The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite rose 0.6%, just shy of the record high set on July 25. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones industrial average moved up 0.3% each.
Among the Dow stocks , Apple ( AAPL ) was unchanged, as the iPhone maker trades about 1% off its record high. The stock's relative strength line remains strong.
Among companies reporting earnings , Foot Locker ( FL ) declined 11% after the athletic-shoe chain's same-store sales missed targets. Friday's fall puts Foot Locker stock back below its 50-day line. Shares had been forming a cup-shaped base.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Veeva Systems ( VEEV ) moved up over 7% after beating the Street's Q2 estimates late Thursday. Shares are extended from a double bottom's 84.34 entry after a breakout on Aug. 10. Veeva stock is at new highs and the relative strength line has followed suit, marking the software stock as a potential leader.
Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) hit another high early Friday, as the stock gained another 2%. Shares are well extended from a 13.95 double-bottom entry.
IPO stock leader BJ's Wholesale Club rose about 3% and is extended beyond the 5% buy range from an IPO base's 27.56 buy point . The 5% buy range tops out at 28.94. Shares surged over 5% Thursday on their way to a breakout. The day's volume was the highest in over a month, signifying institutional demand. Quarterly earnings are due out Aug. 28 before the market open.
IBD 50 stock Palo Alto Networks briefly broke out Thursday above a flat base's 219.48 entry, but faded along with the general market in late-day trade. Shares regained the buy point Friday, breaking out again above the entry. Shares moved up almost 3% and are in the 5% buy range.
Inside The IBD 50 Among the top growth stocks , ServiceNow ( NOW ) is nearing a flat base's 194.91 entry early Friday. Shares moved up over 3%, as they rebound from their 50-day line.
Meanwhile, FANG stock Netflix ( NFLX ) rose 3% after SunTrust Robinson upgraded the stock from hold to buy after its recent pullback. The video streamer remains well below its 50-day line amid the stock's more-than-26% fall from its June 21 high.
